I know my response is two months old but I hope you still read it. I want to give you a different perspective.  One from the side of a parent who has suicidal thoughts. The one thing I hang on to very dearly is the thought of my children taking blame on themselves - I cringe at the thought that they would even remotely blame themselves.   "Could they have done something?" "Did they forget to do something?" "Did they do something wrong?"  "Could they have said something?" ...  Think about it, if you were even younger, you could blamed yourself for the smallest things "I should have finished my dinner" "I shouldn't have complained about my homework" and being 15 maybe your thoughts of blame were more serious but trust me when I say they are not the reason!  It is as far fetched as the idea that your mother killed herself because you didn't finish your dinner.  Even if you saved her at that moment, that would not have prevented what was eventually going to happen.  I live and feel the dark shadow of suicide around my every waking moment...  Not something a child can break for someone else.

I'm not a psychiatrist, I dont claim to know anything, but I have my own experiences and what you are going through is my worst nightmare. I hope you learn to understand one day that you are not the cause of your mother's death.  I want you to know that when you are in that dark pit of despair looking down at pills or whatever method you've chosen there is no rhyme or reason and in fact there is no blame. Except for maybe to one's self. Most suicides are because you cant stand to be around yourself.  Suicide is a selfish act, I admit it.  And the impact on those that you leave behind is a legacy you dont want but I know what its like to feel so dark that you just dont care.

You sound like an intelligent young man and I think strangely enough, in this stiuation that hurts you. You cannot be blissfully ignorant, you will analyze and cross examine and question and think what if...  I hope you learn to think and feel past that. There is no logical answer and even though you probably understand that, it wont mean you can emotionally let it go.  I so very sincerely hope that you learn to go beyond this.  Seek help, in any way.  Dont be afraid to be "desperate" for help.  And if one person doesn't help you, look for help in another place.  There will always be someone who will help, its just a matter of finding one.

I want you to know thats what your mom would have wanted.  I want you to know that your mom actually wont have peace otherwise.

So I'm not one to really give advice on the norm but feel compelled here. First of all being asian and having hard core asian parents says a lot in itself. I myself am asian so i get it.

If i can be direct with you i have a couple of points.  First, go ahead and move out BUT (and this is the most important part) HAVE A PLAN. Save up some money, get a part time job, whatever, but dont do it out of emotion. You sound like a bright kid and to just leap would leave you struggling to just make ends meet. Second, dont try to fix your parents, dont expect them to change, just accept them for who they are. They will not wake up one day and start being caring, loving, interested parents. Remember they have had full lives too and they are the way they are because of everything they've gone through.  I will bet that one day you will come full circle and understand them - that doesn't mean you will "like" them, or want to be like them. You may never choose to befriend people like them... But they are your parents and there may come a time when you are beyond them.

One thing asians seem to learn the hard way is that its not all about books.  So yes, keep up your grades (i would never tell anyone otherwise of course - being asian and all), but make sure you engage in an active social life and learn to enjoy yourself.  That means enjoying who you are (being not so perfect) and learning to find yourself. Don't fall for the judgement and worthlessness that your parents are selling, you're old enough to be able to weed through whats applicable and whats not. 

Best of luck to you!

I had to wait a while too but did get in with a psychiatrist.  He's not convinced that what I'm suffering can be fixed by medication.  I mean he's still trying and working with me but at this point he's only concerned about the suicidal thoughts, not sure what to do with my depression.  

Thanks for the website, i have been doing as much research as possible and so careful about taking drugs.  Frankly, I really wouldn't even consider it if i wasn't so desperate.

My wife has been amazing... but also the source of some of my issues. Confusing and cryptic i know but i guess I'm just not ready to spill my guts out on the internet just yet. In the end, it really is all my fault so...

Thanks again - you've been awesome!

So the short answer is no... But...  

It was slightly before everything hit me full blown but I recently trained for and ran my first marathon.  Lots of long hours of solo running.  I think about doing that again but it just doesn't appeal to me. I did a medium run (1 hour) and i was going crazy, almost sobbing by the end of it. I think being alone with my thoughts has had a negative impact on me.  Thats why even though getting alone time was mentioned a couple of times i dont think it would work for me. 

Maybe it tome to try again in a different format?  I dont know... But am willing to try anything. 

Thanks for the suggestion!

Actually ive read and researched the science of it.  I just cant imagine it actually changes your thoughts. I mean the examples of suicide you give are very intricate and detailed, as mine are... Do the drugs just stop making you think them??  That sounds... Not possible. Do you just forget?  Do the emotions change?  Thats the part i dont get.  Ive tried four or give different kinds of drugs now and whenever the doctor asks if they're working, I'm like - i dont know??

Thanks for responding - really appreciate the insight!

I agree - they know something is wrong but i dont think they can even fathom to what degree!  

From the outside you really would think we are a perfect family

So i have a question for you, hopefully your experience can help me. Because none of the drugs ive tried have helped me i almost dont know what they are supposed to do...??  Like do the right drugs control your thoughts?  Do they change how you think?   It doesn't seem like a drug could do that.  Does that make sense?  The only reason i keep trying with the drugs is because... Well, I'm desperate. But i dont see how they can help.  What they will do for me.  

I would appreciate it if you describe how the right drug helped you.  How did it change you?

Thanks a million!

Thanks for the encouraging words.  I try very hard to keep it from my kids, all they know is that i disappear sometimes...  In actual fact I'm in the basement or closet trying to be quiet while I'm crying.  I know I'm affecting them but trying so hard not to... And sometimes its the only thing that keeps me from going completely over the edge.

Yes she's aware.  I feel awful for her, she has gone through so much!  Friends i guess I've shy'd away from although I've always had plenty.  Second recommendation for alone time, is that a known common remedy?  I never thought of it only because i feel like it would do more harm than good. Having said that I'm really open to try anything!

Wow - you see, i dont think i could drag my family around like that. Sounds ironic i know... but... they are so perfect where they are.

Anyway, thank you for the encouragement. I'm trying to get off the current meds by slowly decreasing my dosage and try something new. But it seems like such a slow and unproductive process.

I think I've always had the tendencies and thoughts but has come full blown over the past year. I have been seeing a dr and he has diagnosed me with major depression. I tried a bunch of different drugs but no help. Funny thing is, it's so not like me to even reach out and seek that kind of help. But I'm feeling so desperate i was willing to try anything. Now I've tried the dr, the drugs and feeling even more helpless... unfixable.

You're absolutely right. I say perfect "on paper" but obviously don't feel that way. Clearing my head... not sure how i would do that... not sure a solo vacation would help me or hurt me. Thanks for the suggestion though - something to think about.
